name: Zhongornis
isnote: Described as a primitive bird (Gao et al. 2008); the cited Wikipedia revision treats it as a primitive maniraptoran of uncertain position.
sum: Small juvenile maniraptoran from the Yixian Formation of Liaoning, China, with a toothless beak.
holotype: The only specimen, a fairly complete juvenile skeleton about 8 cm long on a slab, Yixian Formation, Lingyuan, China.
biology: Had a beaked mouth without teeth; unfused sutures and porous bones show the specimen was a juvenile.
author: Gao et al. 2008

sources.text: C. Gao, L. M. Chiappe, and Q. Meng, J. K. O.'Connor, X. Wang, X. Cheng, J. Liu. 2008. A new basal lineage of Early Cretaceous birds from China and its implications on the evolution of the avian tail. Palaeontology 51(4):775-791
